citations.name: habeas:coverage
citations.commentary:
This private compatibility module only declares the legacy resource and
 selector address shapes; it has no handwritten executable code. Its derived
 serialization and identity operations do not emit source-line measurements.
 The source-tool argument and delivery regressions in `agent/tests.rs`
 exercise these addresses through the legacy adapter. Supported path-based
 address construction is tested separately in `tests/outline_content.rs`.

rationale:
The `habeas:coverage` citation on `crates/trust-but-verify/src/resource.rs` (root) is valid.

- The file is allowed to carry this citation. It sits on a file root, as the built-in requires. The explanation is in fenced citation commentary, so it counts as a tracked justification.
- The commentary agrees with the source. The file holds only `struct[ResourceId]` and `struct[OutlineId]`. Both have derived `Clone`, `Debug`, `PartialEq`, `Eq` and serde traits, and there is no handwritten function body. It is therefore reasonable that no source-line measurements are emitted and the file's 80% instrumented-line threshold is not met.
- The stated test references hold up. The regressions in `agent/tests.rs` build and use `ResourceId` and `OutlineId`. Examples are `source_tools_forward_arguments_and_present_discovery_and_read_results` and `source_reads_track_optional_dependencies_and_empty_searches_remain_discovery`. They go through `SourceTools` and `SourceSession::dispatch`, which parse a `ResourceId` from tool arguments and construct an `OutlineId`. The commentary calls this the legacy adapter. `tests/outline_content.rs` covers path-based address construction, for example `addresses_reconstruct_without_reading_the_file` and `file_constructors_infer_the_language_and_return_addressed_contents`.
- The justification is substantive. It explains why measurement is absent, which is more than saying coverage is hard.
- The file does not also cite the requirement with {impl} or {test} in a way that makes the citation redundant. The `{impl}` markers on the structs are for `requirements.sdk.sources.source_addresses`, which is a different target.
